ideas.title: A motor that starts by itself and drives a fan that sails a paper boat
ideas.critique: This is a real step past 'My first motor', which barely turned. A self-starting three-pole rotor whose speed settles where its torque meets a load solved from the blade shape is new mechanism, and the boat gives the build a visible job. The risk is the chain of jet, sail and boat: if the wind is a fudged push and the film is a fixed shot of a lone device, it falls back to the worn form. Some of the pitched moments are also the familiar recipe of variants side by side with different outcomes (the backwards coil, the stuck two-coil rotor).

ideas.title: My beak carries the weight
ideas.critique: Here Lumi's own body answers physics: a pose that comes from the chain's equilibrium, a Hill-muscle torque limit and a lean over the support polygon. That is something the island has never had, and it ends the long run of objects left alone. It stands or falls on whether the wobble, the braced feet and the drop really come out of the solve. A grip that snaps on, with an IK head trailing it, would be one more puppet animation.

ideas.title: Clams that run my motor
ideas.critique: This is round 1's clam cells again, now seen through the fan rather than a glowing wire, which is a better gauge. The Tafel tiring and recovering at rest is the one fresh touch. It still depends on a motor that has never really run. Made now, it is a row of props and a speed that changes, and power gathered from the player's own plate sizes only matters if those sizes truly come from what they placed.

ideas.title: The friends push my first cart down the dune
ideas.nearest: A snowball that grows as it rolls, a take that misses
ideas.critique: Friends who ride and push a cart the player built is the shareable moment of the big goal itself. Riders shifting the centre of mass, ruts and veering from where the wheels sit is play that comes back, not a wheel let go alone. The weak spot is the friends: if the pushers' forces and the riders climbing aboard are scripted, it becomes a staged ride down a slope, and 'rolls downhill and runs out in sand' is close to the island's rolling films.
